notes.decision: Standard running header 'Of the Teacher' (genitive ⲙ̄- + ⲡⲥⲁⲍ 'the teacher'). The ⲙ̄ⲡ portion is restored from convention; ⲥⲁⲍ is preserved.

Physically preserved word of uncertain meaning. In context of triple parallelism ⲍⲙ ⲡⲍⲣⲁⲩ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲥⲉ ⲍⲙ ⲡⲣ̄..., I have tentatively rendered as 'speech' (suspecting Lyc reduction of ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ 'word/saying'). Alternative readings: 'time' (ⲥⲏⲩ→ⲥⲉ), 'occasion' (ⲥⲉⲡ), or possibly an unidentified sense-domain term. Confidence low.

Translated 'myriads of archons' tentatively. ⲟ̄ⲁⲥ is unattested in our corpus; possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲁⲥⲉ 'multitude' or numerical/quantifier word. Could alternatively be 'voice' (ⲟⲩⲁⲥ) but doesn't fit syntax with ⲛ̄ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ.

Standalone occurrence at end of line 9, with bracketing repetitions in line 11. Most plausibly the kephalaion-numeral 111 (ⲣ=100 + ⲓ=10 + ⲁ=1 with overline indicating numeral) marking either the closing of the previous chapter or the chapter number being inscribed. Preserved untranslated since the numerical reading cannot be confirmed without parallels. Alternative reading: a Greek-derived word ending in -ρία (e.g., τιμωρία 'punishment', τυραννία 'tyranny') that would continue from line 8 ⲉϣⲁⲩⲧⲍⲡⲁ[ⲩ], but the syntactic isolation of line 9 favors the numeral hypothesis.
Same form repeated at start and end of line 11. Likely framing markers around the secondary heading 'in the eye and the hidden fifth.' Preserved untranslated.

Translated 'the fifth' per accumulated glossary (Lyc ⲙⲉϩ-ϯⲟⲩ). Note that this kephalaion treats four types per the heading; the 'fifth which is hidden' likely refers to a hidden faculty/sense beyond the four manifest types — fitting the Manichaean five-faculty register. Could alternatively be 'fourth' (ⲙⲉϩ-ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ) given the four-types theme, but glossary supports 'fifth'.

Reduplicated form of obscure root, translated tentatively as 'watching forth' (continuous/intensive vigilance) given the immediate context of ⲡⲉⲧⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'who watches' in line 18. The reduplication suggests intensive aspect. Could alternatively be a verb of flowing (Greek ῥέω) reduplicated, fitting 'the Living Air' — but watching-vigilance fits the kephalaion's seeing-theme better.

'The Living Air' — Greek ἀήρ retained (cf. Manichaean five Living Elements: aether/wind/light/water/fire). Living-modifier ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ marks it as one of the Living Elements within the cosmic Light substance.
Idiomatic 'pupil of the eye' (literally 'child of the eye'). Coptic ⲧⲁⲗⲟⲩ 'youth, child' used metaphorically for pupil (cf. Hebrew אישון 'little man of the eye'). Standard idiom in this register.

Translated 'the moment(?)' tentatively per accumulated glossary ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ 'this moment'. Alternative: ⲡ̄ⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ 'the spirit' (truncated). Both are plausible in this damaged closing line. Modified by ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ 'who/which lives' suggesting a Living principle.
